title: Parity: out-of-range ASSIGNED_SF handling diverges — C rejects to default SF, Rust/Python clamp to [7,12] boundary
description: Found during 5m15 security review (kimi-k3). For a malformed DIO ASSIGNED_SF byte (e.g. 0 or 200): C gradient.c:318-321 substitutes CONFIG_LICHEN_DEFAULT_SF (reject-to-default), while Rust rf_health.rs adaptive_sf_select and Python ccp.py:346 clamp to the [7,12] boundary (0->7, 200->12). All three are safe individually, but the three implementations can select different SFs for the same malformed DIO — a cross-impl consistency gap if ASSIGNED_SF DIO signaling is ever wired. Options: pick one policy in spec 2a.8 (clamp or reject-to-default) and align all three. Note: Python clamps per ccp.py:346, Rust clamped per 5m15 fix, so C is the odd one out.
